name: Replace an electrical plug
blurb: Wiring a plug correctly — right colours to right terminals, correct fuse, cord grip tight — is a five-minute job that people are needlessly nervous about.
gear: A replacement plug appropriate to your country
The correct fuse rating for the appliance
steps: Unplug the appliance and cut off the old plug entirely so it can never be reused.
Strip the outer sheath carefully without nicking the inner insulation, leaving the earth conductor slightly longer than live and neutral.
Strip each conductor about 6 mm, twist the strands, and identify them by your country’s colour code — in the UK, brown is live, blue is neutral, green-and-yellow is earth.
Connect each to the correct terminal, tighten fully, and check no stray strands escape.
Fit the correct fuse for the appliance — not the biggest one that fits.
Clamp the cord grip on the outer sheath, not the inner cores, and close the plug.
tips: The cord grip must hold the sheath. If it grips only the thin wires, a tug will pull a live conductor loose.
If you are in any doubt about your country’s rules or your own competence, have an electrician do it. Some jurisdictions restrict this work.
proof: A correctly wired plug with the right fuse, a firm cord grip, and an appliance that works.
